headline: Presidential Aide Criticizes Contractor Over Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
metaDescription: A presidential aide spent five hours in traffic on the Lagos-Ibadan expressway and publicly criticized the contractor's scheduling of road works.
aiSummaryBullets: A special aide to President Tinubu experienced a five-hour delay on the Lagos-Ibadan expressway.
The official criticized the road construction contractor for conducting activities during periods of peak traffic.
The incident highlights ongoing logistical challenges and public frustration regarding the major transport corridor.
aiContextParagraph: The Lagos-Ibadan expressway serves as a vital arterial road connecting Nigeria's commercial hub to the rest of the country, frequently experiencing heavy traffic congestion. Recently, Sunday Dare, a special aide to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, became caught in a significant gridlock on this route, reportedly remaining stationary for five hours. Following the delay, the presidential aide issued a public critique directed at the contractor responsible for the construction and maintenance work on the expressway. The official specifically questioned the decision to carry out road improvements during hours when traffic volume is at its highest, suggesting that such timing contributes unnecessarily to the commuting difficulties faced by the public. This event has drawn renewed attention to infrastructure management practices on one of Nigeria's most critical transport links, as regular users continue to navigate prolonged travel times.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained traction due to strong search interest regarding the Lagos-Ibadan expressway, supported by coverage from a prominent independent outlet.
